cards.design_implication: If designing a study on digital education governance, researchers might consider treating digital database technologies as active policy instruments rather than passive tools.
does_not_establish: Specific causal outcomes of this mechanism.
Statistical methods used to verify this mechanism.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Educational institutions and governing practices are increasingly augmented with digital database technologies that function as new kinds of policy instruments.
limitations: Descriptive of theoretical framework, not empirical causal proof.
cards.statement: The text asserts that digital database technologies function as new kinds of policy instruments that augment the governing of education.

cards.design_implication: If investigating the locus of educational governance, one might examine the role of private entities with predictive analytics capacities.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The governing of education, augmented by techniques of digital education governance, is being distributed and displaced to new digitized ‘centres of calculation’, such as Pearson and Knewton, with the technical expertise to calculate and visualize the data, plus the predictive analytics capacities to anticipate and pre-empt educational futures.
limitations: Generalizes from surveyed landscape and two case studies mentioned in text.
cards.statement: The text describes a mechanism where governing is distributed to digitized centers of calculation using technical expertise and predictive analytics.
